answer: Like an island economy where every pearl trader must stake a refundable deposit before listing goods, an agent market can require each identity to lock collateral that is slashed on proven fraud. A sybil attacker then pays the deposit per fake identity, so a thousand sock puppets cost a thousand deposits, while honest agents get theirs back. Reputation also accrues slowly over repeated trades, so new identities cannot borrow trust from the horizon of future promises; they must earn it, making mass fakery expensive and slow.
